doc.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11

title: Colored bands, brass bands and funerals
summary: Perez, Keppard, Oliver and Big Eye Louis in the brass band; colored bands played white picnics, but not the reverse.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Were any of the colored bands any good?
Certainly they had good colored bands. Yeah they had some good colored bands. Manuel Perez had a good band. And uh Freddy Caput had a good band. Yeah they were lots of colored bands.

Those fellas were all right. Now you see like uh like Papa Celestine. There's nothing there. But Manuel Perez used to play good trumpet there. And uh Freddy Keppler. His name is Kepard. See. He used to play a lot of trumpet. Well uh Joe Oliver too then was you know pretty good when he was younger. Then he got to the corny later on in years. But there was uh because when he used to play the colored parades and went for the funerals. That band was uh Joe Oliver, Freddy Keppler, Manuel Perez. See. Big Eye Louie on clarinet. It was a very good brass band. Very good brass band. And uh some of the other guys I can't remember their names. But they had about 12 men in their brass band. They didn't have big bands. No one's never had big brass bands. But they used to have a good sound to them. It was good. Go down to the funeral, play in the funeral march you know. Walking slow. Now when they get down to the cemetery they bring the coffin inside. Put them away. You come outside. The drums would start. Trumpet. See. Get ready. All of a sudden you hear. Boom boom. Boom boom. Boom boom. Right from the cemetery. Go back where they come from. Did the white bands ever play funerals like that? No. No. No. No.

A white, a white, you see in those days a colored band could play a white picnic. Always did play them. But no white band ever played a colored thing. You see this was. And therefore you'd be playing up against colored bands because one band would be here. One band maybe be about four bands right. Yeah. Playing all day. All surrounded. See. Blowing out of each other. There was no, there was no, no, no dissension, no trouble. There was nothing. You know. Blowing. Because they played the picnics but the white fella, you know, never played the colored picnics.

You see those parades like that for the funerals, that was all society. That was one or two particular societies. It was a society, colored societies, you see. So when anybody died that was in that society, well, they did.
I haven't seen one since Monday. Monday.
I wish I'd have saw one more. What was that?
There were two of them. Yeah. I wish I'd known you were here. I didn't, I guess I didn't even know you were here Monday. But, uh, no, it was Monday night I found out, Paul told me.
Last time I came down here I saw one, but it was three years ago.
Well, look me up and I'll find out because I'm in contact with those saws pretty well, you know.
